column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: “Do not envy one another, do not inflate prices against one another, do not hate one another,

do not turn your backs on one another, and do not undercut one another in selling. Be, O servants of Allah, brothers. The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him, forsake him, lie to him or hold him in contempt.
Taqwā is here”—and he pointed to his chest three times. “It is evil enough for a person to hold his Muslim brother in contempt.
All of the Muslim is inviolable to the Muslim: his blood, his wealth and his honour.” Reported by Muslim.
Lā taḥāsadū (“do not envy one another”): let none of you envy another.
Wa-lā tanājashū (“do not inflate prices against one another”): let none of you raise the price of an item he does not want to buy,
in order to deceive someone else who wants it.
Wa-lā tabāghaḍū (“do not hate one another”): do not engage in the causes of mutual hatred.
Wa-lā tadābarū (“do not turn your backs on one another”): let none of you turn his back on his brother when he meets him, cutting him off.

“And do not undercut one another in selling”: by saying to someone who has bought an item, during the option period: Cancel this sale and I will sell you the like of it for less than its price, or something better for its price;

or when the two parties to a sale have settled the price between them and agreed, and only the contract remains, and he offers more, or offers it for less. This is after the price has been settled; before agreement, it is not unlawful.

“Be, O servants of Allah, brothers”: this is like a reason for what preceded; that is, treat one another as brothers in affection, gentleness, compassion, kindness, cooperation in good and the like, with pure hearts.
“The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim”: because one religion unites them; the Exalted said: “The believers are but brothers” [al-Ḥujurāt 49:10].
“He does not wrong him”: he does not bring harm upon him in his person, religion, honour or wealth without legal warrant.
“Or forsake him”: he does not abandon the support that is due to him in the Sharīʿah, because among the rights of the brotherhood of Islam is mutual support.

Wa-lā yakdhibuhu (“or lie to him”): with fatḥah on the yāʾ of the present tense and a light dhāl with kasrah, according to the better-known reading; it is also permissible to put ḍammah on its first letter and sukūn on its second (yukdhibuhu). [It means] he does not tell him anything contrary to the facts.

Wa-lā yaḥqiruhu (“or hold him in contempt”): with the undotted ḥāʾ and the qāf; he does not belittle his standing or lower his worth, for when Allah created him He did not hold him in contempt, but raised him, addressed him and gave him responsibility.
Al-taqwā (“taqwā”): guarding against the punishment of Allah by doing what is commanded and leaving what is prohibited.
“It is evil enough for a person”: it suffices him as evil.
ʿIrḍuhu (“his honour”): his standing, that is, his merits and the merits of his forefathers; it may also mean his person.
The prohibition of envy, mutual hatred, turning one's back on one another and undercutting one another in selling.
The prohibition of harming a Muslim in any way, by word or deed.
The prohibition of misguiding whims, because they bring about mutual hatred.

The command to acquire whatever makes the Muslims brothers in every respect. Included in this is fulfilling the rights of a Muslim over a Muslim, such as returning and initiating the greeting of peace, responding to one who sneezes, visiting the sick, following funerals, accepting invitations and giving sincere advice.
The prohibition of injustice.
Among the rights of a Muslim over a Muslim is supporting him when he needs it, whether in a worldly matter, such as being able to ward off an enemy who wants to attack him—

then he must ward him off—or in a religious matter, such as being able to counsel him away from his error, by admonition and the like; then he must give the counsel, and leaving it is the unlawful forsaking.

A warning against holding a Muslim in contempt, for Allah did not hold him in contempt when He created him; He subjected to him what is in the heavens and the earth, called him Muslim, believer and servant, and made Muḥammad ﷺ the Messenger from Him to him.
So whoever holds a Muslim in contempt has held in contempt what Allah the Exalted has honoured.
The core of taqwā is what is in the heart of the magnification of Allah, fear of Him and awareness of His watching; mere righteous deeds without that are of no account.
The inviolability of the blood, wealth and honour of the Muslims.
